articles.text:

Databricks discusses funding round at $225 billion valuation — Channel NewsAsia
Fedir Kryshtovskyi
21

Databricks, a developer of software for working with data and artificial intelligence, is holding preliminary talks to raise several billion dollars. The new funding round could value the company at about $225 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Deal terms may change
As Channel NewsAsia reports , The Wall Street Journal published this information on November 20. The talks are ongoing, and the terms of the potential deal may still change. Databricks did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
Previous round and products
In August, Databricks said it had raised $5 billion at a valuation of $190 billion. The company was founded in 2013; it develops software products for storing, managing and analyzing data, as well as for building artificial intelligence applications.
Databricks competes with Snowflake, and the company is considered a candidate for a future stock market listing. Databricks previously said that the annual revenue run rate of its Lakebase product exceeded $100 million, while the figure for its Lakehouse data warehousing business reached more than $1.5 billion.

articles.title: Oracle OpenAI Contract Fully Funded After $20B Raise
articles.snippet: Oracle OpenAI Contract Fully Funded After $20B Raise shattered.io

Oracle Says OpenAI Deal Is Funded After $20B Raise
Priya Anand
Updated Nov 22, 2026 · 16 min read
Photo: Peter Kaminski from San Francisco, California, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Oracle told investors on November 20, 2026 that it has locked down the money for its OpenAI infrastructure contract. In the company’s own words, “Oracle has secured all the funding we need to fulfill our contract with OpenAI.” The statement landed after a final capital raise earlier in November, and it aims to settle a question that has hung over the Oracle OpenAI contract for months: who pays for the servers, the buildings and the power?
Table of Contents
What Oracle Actually Said on November 20
The $20 Billion Raise: $10 Billion in Stock, $10 Billion in Debt
What the Securities Filing Says and Leaves Out
Closing date: November 4, 2026
Use of proceeds: general corporate purposes
Vendor Financing and the Investor Day Plan
Why “Fully Funded” Does Not Mean Fully Paid For
The Unknown: What the OpenAI Contract Is Worth
What Oracle Said, in Its Own Words
How Oracle’s Funding Claim Compares With Other AI Spenders
Historical Context: Cloud Buildouts and the Cost of Capacity
Market Impact: Investors, Lenders and Suppliers
Why This Matters for the AI Models Race
What Could Still Go Wrong
Five Predictions for the Next Two Quarters
Frequently Asked Questions
What did Oracle announce about its OpenAI contract?
How much did Oracle raise?
Is the $20 billion reserved for OpenAI?
How much is the OpenAI contract worth?
What is vendor financing?
Is Oracle really the first fully funded hyperscaler?
Does the funding guarantee OpenAI will get its capacity on time?
Related
The raise totaled $20 billion, split roughly evenly between $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in debt. Oracle also called itself the first hyperscaler fully funded for this investment cycle. That is a bold claim in a year when capital markets have been testing every AI spender, including Anthropic, which priced its IPO at $83 and raised $81.31 billion according to our earlier coverage.
This analysis separates what Oracle confirmed from what it did not. The company gave two headline numbers, one date and a handful of carefully worded sentences. It did not give the contract’s total value, its length or its payment schedule. Those gaps matter as much as the confirmed facts, and we treat them that way throughout.

What Oracle Actually Said on November 20
Oracle’s message came in a few short statements, and each one does a specific job. The first states the conclusion: the money needed for the OpenAI contract is secured. The second explains how Oracle got there, pointing to a final capital raise earlier in the month. The third tries to head off a different worry, that Oracle still needs extra help from suppliers to finish the job.
On that third point, Oracle said any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options. It added that its ability to deliver on the OpenAI contract does not depend on those discussions. Read together, the statements frame vendor talks as optional upside rather than a missing piece of the plan.

The post Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:49 PM
Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs
Lockheed Martin received five directly valued defense awards totaling approximately $2.35 billion, along with positions on two large multiple-award contract vehicles whose shared ceilings cannot be assigned to any individual contractor.
The largest direct award is a Navy letter-contract modification valued at up to $1.53 billion for Trident II D5 missile production and deployed-systems support. The sole-source effort will continue through September 2031.
Aircraft Production And Sustainment
The company received a $330.6 million modification for long-lead materials supporting 75 Lot 22 F-35 aircraft. The full amount was obligated at award, with work continuing through December 2030.
A separate $93.2 million order covers F-35 depot test equipment, cybersecurity upgrades, repair capacity, technical data, and engineering support. The Navy, Air Force, and cooperative-program partners obligated the complete order value.
The Air Force also awarded Lockheed Martin a $316.6 million C-5 Galaxy logistics-support contract. Approximately $23.7 million was initially obligated for supply-chain, repair, engineering, and technical services.
A $72.6 million F-35 Block 4 modification increases the ceiling for software, cybersecurity, and program-management work, but no funding was obligated at award.
Lockheed Martin was additionally selected for the Navy’s shared $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program vehicle and the Air Force’s $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Enterprise vehicle. Those ceilings represent pools available to all selected contractors and are not included in Lockheed Martin’s $2.35 billion direct-award total.

articles.title: Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom
articles.snippet: Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom Seoul Economic Daily
articles.text:
Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom
Funds From National Growth Fund to Expand Jeungpyeong, Gimcheon Plants
CCL Plant Utilization Already Above 100%
New Production Lines and R&D Center Planned
Semiconductor Value Chain From Materials to Back-End Nears Completion
Market Signal |
Published 2026.11.22. 20:13:03 |
By Kim Byung-joon econ_jun@sedaily.com
| Summary | Save
A A A
This article appeared on Signal, the capital markets compass, at 2:13 p.m. on Nov. 22, 2026.
View of Doosan's headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Doosan
Doosan (000150) is raising 500 billion won ($340 million) from the National Growth Fund to expand its copper clad laminate (CCL) production plants, responding to a surge in demand for high-value CCL driven by expanding investment in artificial intelligence data centers. Analysts say Doosan Group is completing a semiconductor value chain that now spans semiconductor materials, wafers — the discs on which chips are built — through its acquisition of SK Siltron, and back-end processing at Doosan Tesna.
Doosan's domestic CCL production lines are already running above 100% utilization, leaving the company in need of added capacity through expansion, according to investment banking sources on the 22nd. "The company will raise funds from the National Growth Fund and the Korea Development Bank and invest in domestic plants, excluding China," one investment banking source said.
This is not Doosan's first expansion plan. The company previously announced it would invest 400 billion won by 2028 to build a CCL production facility for optical modules spanning about 33,000 square meters next to its flexible copper clad laminate (FCCL) plant in Gimje, Jeonbuk State. Adding the expansion of the Jeungpyeong plant through low-interest loans from the National Growth Fund is seen as a move to respond quickly to rapidly rising CCL demand. Unlike Gimje, which requires new construction, the Jeungpyeong and Gimcheon expansions can be completed relatively quickly.
Demand for CCL used in optical modules is surging as AI data centers proliferate and networks shift to ultra-high speeds of 800G and above. Optical modules convert electrical signals between servers and network equipment into light signals, and CCL is a core material for printed circuit boards. Securities analysts said rising demand for optical module CCL is creating a seller's market. "With a CCL supply shortage expected to persist for the next two to three years, suppliers are likely to secure favorable pricing terms when signing long-term supply contracts," said Kim Min-kyung, an analyst at Hana Securities.
Doosan also plans to build a research and development center in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province. Doosan Group had initially planned to build an advanced technology R&D center focused on hydrogen research involving Doosan Enerbility, Doosan Fuel Cell and Doosan Mobility Innovation, but it is now expected to extend the center's scope to semiconductor R&D. The move aims to upgrade and strengthen technological competitiveness as the group completes its semiconductor value chain. Under the structure, SK Siltron produces wafers, the starting point of chip manufacturing, Doosan supplies CCL, and Doosan Tesna handles back-end processes such as wafer testing and package testing for system semiconductors. The Korea Development Bank, together with Woori Bank, earlier arranged 2.5 trillion won in acquisition financing for the SK Siltron purchase.

articles.title: Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
articles.snippet:
Raytheon received three directly valued Navy awards totaling approximately $159.4 million for Rolling Airframe Missile and Cooperative Engagement Capability work.
The post Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:42 PM
Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
Raytheon received three directly valued Navy awards totaling approximately $159.4 million for Rolling Airframe Missile and Cooperative Engagement Capability work.
The largest award is a $120.3 million firm-fixed-price modification covering production of Rolling Airframe Missile Block 2B guided-missile round packs.
Missile Production And Engineering
The Block 2B modification supports Navy production and a Foreign Military Sales requirement for Japan. The Navy obligated $105.6 million, while Japan provided $14.7 million. Work will take place in Germany, Arizona, West Virginia, Great Britain, Ohio, and other U.S. locations through February 2030.
Raytheon also received a $12.3 million modification for design-agent and engineering support for the Rolling Airframe Missile system. Germany funded the complete award, which includes systems engineering, software maintenance, reliability, quality-assurance, logistics, and technical support through September 2028.
A separate $26.7 million modification supports the Cooperative Engagement Capability weapon system. The work includes design, development, integration, testing, and maintenance for the United States, Australia, Japan, and Canada. The full amount was obligated at award.
Raytheon was also named to the Navy’s shared $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program contract and parent company RTX was selected for the Air Force’s $16.1 billion propulsion vehicle. Neither shared ceiling is included in Raytheon’s direct-award total because future task orders will determine actual revenue.

Средства направят на увеличение числа доступных рынков и повышение лимитов открытого интереса на платформе Omni.
$30 млн — Nomad. Бразильский финтех-стартап привлек средства в рамках раунда серии C под руководством Tether Capital при участии Endeavor, Globo Ventures, Tiger Global Management и Spark Capital. $25 млн — Avenia (ранее BRLA Digital). Бразильская финтех-компания завершила расширенный раунд серии A под руководством Lightspeed Faction при участии Flourish Ventures, Quona Capital, Big Bets, Headline Asia, Fluent Ventures, Tomorrow Capital и Patria Investments. Компания специализируется на трансграничных расчетах. Она также выпускает стейблкоин BRLA, привязанный к местной валюте. Средства направят на запуск новых продуктов и приобретение лицензированных финансовых организаций.
$10 млн — MetaComp. Платежный сервис привлек финансирование в рамках расширенного раунда Pre-Series A+ при участии Tether и Further Asset Management. Компания обслуживает трансграничные переводы в фиатных валютах и стейблкоинах. Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas (CAM) advised Multiples Alternate Asset Management Private Limited on its investment in jewellery brand GIVA , as part of a funding round of approximately $100 million (around ₹900 crore) led by Multiples Equity .
The transaction involving Indiejewels Fashion Private Limited , which operates GIVA, comprised a combination of fresh issuance of securities and purchase of securities from certain existing shareholders.
The CAM transaction team was led by partners Aditi Manchanda and Abhishek Kalra, with support from principal associate Chandni Ochani and associate Rajat Pareek.
The legal due diligence was undertaken by the transaction team along with senior associate Kaushik Raichura and associates Rhea Prasad and Twinkle Tiwari.
The firm's intellectual property diligence was led by Swati Sharma, partner and head of intellectual property, with support from principal associate-designate Andri Shukla and principal associate Rohin Koolwal.
Sowmya Kumar, partner, led the employment diligence, supported by Luv Saggi, director – employment, senior associate Soumyashree Chowdhury and associate Saksham Kumar.
Arya Tripathy, partner, assisted on information technology and data privacy due diligence, with support from associate Milind Yadav.
The investment marks another funding round for GIVA, a jewellery brand operating in India's growing organised jewellery market.
